name: TCI Islander Status -- Grant to BOTC/British Citizens and Registered BOTC

requirement_groups.name: BOTC of TCI, or British Citizen with PRC/long residence

requirements.blocker_text: Must be a British Overseas Territories Citizen of TCI, or a British Citizen.
If applying as a British Citizen (not already a TCI BOTC): must have held a PRC for at least 5 years, OR have been legally resident in TCI for at least 10 years.
Must have no criminal record or bankruptcy in any country.

requirement_groups.name: Registered BOTC under Section 15(4) of the British Nationality Act 1981

requirements.blocker_text: Must have been born in the Islands, with both parents holding legal status at the time of the applicant's birth.
Requires at least 10 years of legal residence.

evidence_required.document: Proof of BOTC/British citizenship or Section 15(4) registration
Police clearance (no criminal record/bankruptcy, all countries)

sources.title: Government of the Turks and Caicos Islands -- TCI Islander Status: acquisition by grant, BOTC/British Citizen route and registered-BOTC (Section 15(4) BNA 1981) route, annual June-September application window, Islander Status Commission review, public-interest/economic-impact assessment criteria, fee schedule

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the Turks and Caicos Islands' initial build. This route is for people who are ALREADY a British Overseas Territories Citizen or British Citizen (often via a PRC route -- see the tc_prc_*.json files, which are prerequisites here) but want the additional, higher-tier TCI Islander status itself (voting rights, Crown land, scholarships) -- it is emphatically NOT the BOTC naturalisation route (see tc_naturalisation_botc.json), which grants citizenship rather than local status. Two OR-groups folded into one file since both lead to the same TCI Status grant on the same application, differing only in the applicant's starting citizenship/status. application_window reflects the source's explicit June 1 - September 30 annual window for these (non-marriage) grant applications -- contrasted with tc_islander_status_marriage.json, which the same source states may be submitted at any time. Assessment also weighs public interest, economic impact on existing workers, and whether the applicant offers exceptional skills -- these qualitative criteria are noted here but not separately modelled as hard requirements since no quantifiable threshold was given.
